ITQAN:v4p427/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p427/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ITQAN:v4p427/r5.claim: ʿAlī says the Prophet’s household instead identifies ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى, referring to intercession.
ITQAN:v4p427/r5.anchor: لكنا أهل البيت نقول أن أرجى آية في كتاب الله ﴿ ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى ﴾ وهي الشفاعة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.claim: The discourse moves from day and night as models of developmental trials, to reassurance, promised better times, examples of past divine help, and duties arising from those favours.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.anchor: Following is the sequence of the discourse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.claim: The future success promised to the Prophet is followed by reminders of earlier deliverance and spiritual blessing, then guidance to fulfil the duties those favours impose.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.anchor: At the end, he is guided to fulfil the obligations

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r4.claim: The unstated object of “give” is the promised good of verse 4; it is suppressed because the triumphs were still future, while the wording promises the Prophet’s pleasure.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r4.anchor: that he will become very happy

QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r9.claim: When asked whether he would be satisfied with a gift apart from the Giver, Muhammad answered that he would not.
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r9.anchor: قيل : أفترضى بالعطاء عن المعطي ؟ قال : لا

FARRA:v3p273#2/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p273#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v3p273#2/r3.claim: ʿAbd Allāh's reading wa-la-sayuʿṭīka has the same meaning as the standard reading.

FARRA:v3p273#2/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p273#2/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p273#2/r4.claim: The form sa-yuʿṭīka is a colloquial contraction of sawfa, which has become frequent enough to lose initial fa and wāw; other expressions show similar shortening.
FARRA:v3p273#2/r4.anchor: إلا أن (سوف) كثرت في الكلام، وعرف موضعها، فترك منها الفاء والواو،

FARRA:v3p273#2/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p273#2/r5.speaker: شاعر
FARRA:v3p273#2/r5.claim: An unnamed poet omits the fāʾ from kayfa in a line meaning “how would they not detect a trace?”, attesting the contraction.
FARRA:v3p273#2/r5.anchor: قال الشاعر : من طالبين لبعران لنا رفضت ... كيلا يحسون من بعراننا أثرا

BINTSHATI:v1p38/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r3.claim: Verse 5 completes the reassurance: God did not leave the Prophet in the past, and his future is better.
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r3.anchor: يتكامل بها التجلي الإلهي على المصطفى: ما تركك فيما مضى، وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى

BINTSHATI:v1p38/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r4.claim: The promised gift is deliberately left unrestricted; the Prophet needs only the gift that satisfies him, and commentators should not define it by their own preferences.
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r4.anchor: فحسب الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - الإعطاء الذي يرضيه، وليس وراء الرضى مطمح

BINTSHATI:v1p38/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r5.claim: Al-Tabari transmits from Ibn Abbas that the promised gift is a palace in Paradise with spouses and servants; later exegetes add material details, which the author declines to impose.
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r5.anchor: إنه ألفقصر في الجنة، في كل قصر ما ينبغي من الأزواج والخدم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r6.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the predestination discussion could cause fear, so God reassured His dearest servant by recounting his favor and the good of both lives.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r6.anchor: أنس تعالى أحب عباده إليه وأعظمهم منزلة لديه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r3.claim: Some servants gain clear insight through steadfast piety and reflection, moving from inference to direct recognition of the path.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r3.anchor: بل قد يطلع سبحانه خواص عباده - بملازمته التقوى والاعتبار - على واضحة السبيل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r4.speaker: النبي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r4.claim: The Prophet told Ḥāritha, and similarly Abū Bakr, that he had found the truth and should remain firm in it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r4.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لحارثة : ( وجدت فالزم ) وقال مثله للصديق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r5.claim: The faithful receive good news in both lives and angelic reassurance, walking by a light God grants them.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r5.anchor: لهم البشرى في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r6.claim: The surah’s consolation is linked to promises of angels’ protection and God-given light and discernment.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r7.claim: The author compares guided believers to someone brought from death into light, unlike one trapped in darkness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r7.anchor: أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به

BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r8.claim: The faithful gain clear insight through piety, detach from worldly hopes, and prepare for the afterlife through excellent deeds.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r8.anchor: فقطعوا عن الدنيا الآمال , وتأهبوا لآخرتهم بأوضح الأعمال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p455/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455/r2.claim: The many human paths reduce to belief or disbelief and to Paradise or Hell, as paired creation and flight toward God indicate.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455/r2.anchor: ولانحصار السبل وإن تشعبت في طريقي

NAHHAS:v5p249/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p249/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p249/r10.claim: The ʿAbd Allāh reading wasi-yuʿṭīka and the common reading fa-sayuʿṭīka have the same meaning for Sibawayh; al-Farrāʾ explains the missing conjunctions by colloquial deletion.
NAHHAS:v5p249/r10.anchor: وفي حرف عبد الله ( وسيعطيك ) وهما واحد عند سيبويه

NAHHAS:v5p249/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p249/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p249/r11.claim: The second object is omitted, as when one says ‘I gave Zayd’ without specifying the gift.
NAHHAS:v5p249/r11.anchor: قال أبو جعفر حذف المفعول الثاني كما تقول أعطيت زيدا ولا تبين العطية

DURR-FULL:v8p541/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r6.speaker: أم حفص
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r6.claim: A dead puppy hidden beneath the Prophet's bed delayed revelation for four days; after Khawla found it, the Prophet trembled and the passage through ‘you will be satisfied’ came down.
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة في مسنده والطبراني وابن مردويه عن أم حفص عن أمها

DURR-FULL:v8p541/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r8.claim: Shown the community's successive conquests, the Prophet rejoiced; God then promised him a thousand pearl palaces with musk soil, spouses, and servants.
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r8.anchor: وابن مردويه وأبو نعيم كلاهما في الدلائل عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r13.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r13.claim: Most interpreters take God's promised gift and the Prophet's satisfaction as referring to the Hereafter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r13.anchor: قال جمهور الناس: ذلك في الآخرة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r14.speaker: بعضهم من أهل البيت
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r14.claim: Some members of the Prophet's family call it the Qur'an's most hopeful verse because he will not accept a member of his community remaining in Hell.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r14.anchor: وقال بعضهم من أهل البيت هذه أرجى آية في كتاب الله تعالى لأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يرضى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet's satisfaction means no member of his family enters Hell.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: رضاه أن لا يدخل أحد من أهل بيته في النار،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r2.claim: Another Ibn Abbas explanation is God's promise of a thousand palaces in Paradise and their needed blessings and attendants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا: رضاه أن الله تعالى وعده بألف قصر في الجنة بما يحتاج إليه من النعم والخدم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r3.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r3.claim: Some scholars say his satisfaction is also granted in this life through the conquest of Mecca and similar victories.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r3.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء رضاه في الدنيا بفتح مكة وغيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r4.claim: Ibn Masud's codex reads wa-la-sawfa yuʿtika, using an emphatic form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r4.anchor: وفي مصحف ابن مسعود: «ولسيعطيك ربك فترضى» ،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r18.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r18.claim: The Prophet says he would not be satisfied while anyone of his community remained in Hell.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r18.anchor: «إذا لا أرضى وأحد من أمتي في النار» ،

TABATABAI:93:3-7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r5.claim: The promise of a gift that will satisfy him reaffirms that the afterlife is better; it promises an unrestricted gift followed by unrestricted satisfaction.
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r5.anchor: تقرير وتثبيت لقوله { وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى } وقد اشتمل الوعد

TABATABAI:93:3-7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r6.claim: Another view says the promise looks to both lives rather than only the afterlife.
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r6.anchor: وقيل الآية ناظرة إلى الحياتين جميعا دون الحياة الآخرة فقط

TABATABAI:93:1-11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:1-11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:93:1-11/r1.claim: A quoted statement says God chose the Hereafter over the world for the Prophet's household and connects that choice to the promise that the Prophet will be satisfied.
TABATABAI:93:1-11/r1.anchor: إنا أهل بيت اختار الله لنا الآخرة على الدنيا

TABATABAI:93:1-11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:1-11/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TABATABAI:93:1-11/r2.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet saw Fatima grinding grain in a rough camel-hair garment and urged her to endure worldly bitterness for the next life's blessing; God then revealed 93:5. The author allows that this verse descended later as an insertion or was revealed again alone.
TABATABAI:93:1-11/r2.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال دخل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم على فاطمة وهي تطحن بالرحى

TABATABAI:93:1-11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:1-11/r3.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:93:1-11/r3.claim: Through Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya, ʿAli reports the Prophet affirming that the intercession discussed by the Iraqis is true; the excerpt breaks before the rest of the report.
TABATABAI:93:1-11/r3.anchor: حدثني عمي محمد بن الحنفية عن علي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

THALABI:v10p223/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p223/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p223/r12.claim: God will grant the Prophet reward; another interpretation says He grants victory, power, and a growing community of believers.
THALABI:v10p223/r12.anchor: ولسوف يعطيك ربك من الثواب، وقيل: من النصر والتمكن وكثرة المؤمنين

THALABI:v10p223/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p223/r13.speaker: علي بن عبد الله بن عباس عن النبي
THALABI:v10p223/r13.claim: The Prophet says he saw the conquests that would come to his community, and the verse promised him a thousand pearl palaces in Paradise, with musk soil.
THALABI:v10p223/r13.anchor: عن علي بن عبد الله بن عباس [عن أبيه] قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «رأيت ما هو مفتوح على أمتي من بعدي كفرا كفرا»

THALABI:v10p224/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p224/r1.speaker: السدي عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p224/r1.claim: He says Muhammad's satisfaction means that none of his family will enter the Fire.
THALABI:v10p224/r1.anchor: عن السدي، عن ابن عباس: في قوله ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى قال: رضا محمد أن لا يدخل أحد من أهل بيته النار

THALABI:v10p224/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p224/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p224/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes the promise as intercession for all believers.
THALABI:v10p224/r2.anchor: وقيل: هي الشفاعة في جميع المؤمنين

THALABI:v10p224/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p224/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي
THALABI:v10p224/r3.claim: The Prophet says he will intercede for his community until God says He is pleased and he replies that he is pleased; the report calls this the most hopeful verse for the Prophet's household.
THALABI:v10p224/r3.anchor: عن أبيه علي بن أبي طالب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «أشفع لأمتي حتى ينادي ربي عز وجل: رضيت يا محمد

THALABI:v10p224#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p224#2/r1.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v10p224#2/r1.claim: In response to his tears and plea for his community, God tells Gabriel to reassure Muhammad that He will satisfy him concerning his community and not grieve him.
THALABI:v10p224#2/r1.anchor: فقال الله سبحانه: يا جبرائيل اذهب إلى محمد، فقل: إنا سنرضيك في أمتك ولا نسوؤك

THALABI:v10p224#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p224#2/r2.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v10p224#2/r2.claim: A report says that after this verse was revealed, he vowed not to be satisfied while one member of his community remained in the Fire.
THALABI:v10p224#2/r2.anchor: ويروي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لما نزلت هذه الآية: «إذا لا أرضى وواحد من أمتي في النار»

THALABI:v10p224#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p224#2/r3.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
THALABI:v10p224#2/r3.claim: Seeing Fatima grind and nurse in a rough camel-hide garment, the Prophet comforts her by pointing to the promised sweetness of the afterlife and citing the verse.
THALABI:v10p224#2/r3.anchor: دخل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على فاطمة رضي الله عنها وعليها كساء من جلد الإبل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:1-5/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:1-5/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:1-5/r4.claim: A report says the Prophet vowed not to be satisfied while one member of his community remained in the Fire.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:1-5/r4.anchor: يروى أنه قال عليه السلام لما نزلت هذه الآية: إذن لا أرضى وواحد من أمتي في النار.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p414/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p414/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p414/r1.claim: Ītāʾ is broader than ʿaṭāʾ and includes material or immaterial grants; it may be withdrawn and does not always imply the recipient may dispose of it, whereas a gift belongs to its recipient to use freely.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p414/r1.anchor: الإيتاء يكون لأمور مادية وغيرها (الملك، الحكمة، الذكر)

BURSEVI:v10p351/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p351/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p351/r1.claim: God did not stop the inward flow of prophethood and messengership or the inward flow of sainthood to the Prophet.
BURSEVI:v10p351/r1.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : ما ودعك ربك بقطع فيض النبوة والرسالة

BURSEVI:v10p351/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p351/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p351/r3.claim: The lam is emphatic lam of initiation, not an oath; the suppressed subject is You, and lam plus سوف assures a gift certain to arrive after a wise delay.
BURSEVI:v10p351/r3.anchor: اللام للابتداء دخلت الخبر لتأكيد مضمون الجملة والمبتدأ محذوف تقديره ولأنت

BURSEVI:v10p351/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p351/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p351/r4.claim: The Prophet's final spiritual states are better and more complete than his initial acts, as the completion of religion indicates.

BURSEVI:v10p351/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p351/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p351/r5.claim: The promise includes worldly gifts such as perfected character, knowledge, public success, conquests, and Islam's spread under the Prophet and later Muslim rulers, as well as unknown honors stored for him.
BURSEVI:v10p351/r5.anchor: والآية عدة كريمة شاملة لما أعطاه الله في الدنيا من كمال النفس وعلوم الأولين

BURSEVI:v10p351/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p351/r6.speaker: رسول الله عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p351/r6.claim: The Prophet described a thousand white-pearl palaces in Paradise, with musk for soil.
BURSEVI:v10p351/r6.anchor: وقد أنبأ عنسمة منها قوله عليه اسلام لي في الجنة ألف قصر من لؤلؤ أبيض

QASHANI:93:4-8/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:93:4-8/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:93:4-8/r2.claim: After pure annihilation, the Lord gives the Prophet true divine existence to guide creation and call to truth; he is satisfied because that gift restores existence.
QASHANI:93:4-8/r2.anchor: الوجود الحقاني لهداية الخلق والدعوة إلى الحق بعد هذا الفناء الصرف

SULAMI:v2p400#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#4/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p400#4/r1.claim: God offers the Prophet a gift, but his lofty aspiration is not satisfied by anything in the created worlds (68:4).
SULAMI:v2p400#4/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : كأنه يقول لنبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God will give Muhammad a thousand pearl palaces in Paradise, with musk soil and suitable spouses and servants, until he is content.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : فانزل الله ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى فاعطاه في الجنة الف قصر من لؤلؤ

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443/r2.claim: Qatada says the promised giving is Paradise on the Day of Resurrection.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443/r2.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى قال : ذلك يوم القيامة هي الجنة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443/r3.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the promised giving as intercession.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443/r3.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه انه سئل عن قوله : ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى قال : هي الشفاعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r4.claim: The clause is an independent continuation of the opening oath clauses, not its answer: after denying abandonment, it reassures that the Prophet's ending will surpass his beginning in this life and the next.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r4.anchor: والجملة معطوفة على الجمل الابتدائية وليست معطوفة على جملة جواب القسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes both lām particles as lām al-ibtidāʾ and supplies an omitted subject in the second clause: 'You will surely be given by your Lord.'
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r1.anchor: جزم صاحب ( الكشاف ) بأنه لام الابتداء وقدر مبتدأ محذوفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r2.speaker: ابن الحاجب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r2.claim: Ibn al-Hajib regards the lām in 'your Lord will give you' as the emphatic lām answering an oath; Ibn Hisham agrees, apparently because the future particle prevents nūn of emphasis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r2.anchor: واختار ابن الحاجب أن اللام في { ولسوف يعطيك ربك } لام التوكيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur questions the claim that the future particle itself forces the lām to be an oath-response lām.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r3.anchor: وأقول في كون وجود حرف التنفيس يوجب كون اللام لام جواب قسم محل نظر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#3/r1.claim: God will give the Prophet abundant good in the afterlife, leaving him content with what he receives.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#3/r1.anchor: في الآخرة من الخير فترضى بما تعطى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#3/r2.speaker: علي والحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#3/r2.claim: They explain the promised gift as the Prophet's intercession for his community until he is satisfied.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#3/r2.anchor: قال علي والحسن هو الشفاعة في أمته حتى يرضى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet grieved after being shown successive future openings for his community, so God revealed this promise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#3/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس عرض على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما يفتح على أمته من بعده كفرا كفرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r1.claim: God will satisfy Muhammad in the Hereafter through his community and the honor prepared for him, including al-Kawthar with pearl-dome banks and fragrant musk soil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r1.anchor: في الدار الآخرة يعطيه حتى يرضيه في أمته، وفيما أعده له من الكرامة، ومن جملته نهر الكوثر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet was shown treasures opening for his community and was given a million Paradise palaces, each with suitable spouses and servants. Ibn Kathir calls the chain sound to Ibn Abbas and says such a report is only by transmitted authority.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r2.anchor: عن علي بن عبد الله بن عباس عن أبيه قال: عرض على رسول الله ما هو مفتوح على أمته من بعده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muhammad's satisfaction includes that none of his family enter the Fire.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r3.anchor: وقال السدي، عن ابن عباس: من رضاء محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ألا يدخل أحد من أهل بيته النار.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r4.speaker: الحسن، أبو جعفر الباقر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r4.claim: Al-Hasan and Abu Ja'far al-Baqir explain the promised gift as intercession.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن: يعني بذلك الشفاعة. وهكذا قال أبو جعفر الباقر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r5.claim: The Prophet says God chose the Hereafter over this world for his household, in connection with the promise of satisfaction.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#3/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أنا أهل بيت اختار الله لنا الآخرة على الدنيا

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r12.claim: A report says the Prophet was shown his community's conquests and was pleased, then the promise that God would give until he was pleased was revealed.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r12.anchor: أريت فتوح أمتي فرضيت، فنزل: (ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى).

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r3.claim: The promise includes worldly victories from Badr and Mecca through later Muslim conquests and the spread of Islam, and God's reserved reward in the hereafter.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r3.anchor: موعد شامل لما أعطاه في الدنيا من الفلج والظفر بأعدائه يوم بدر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet will have a thousand white pearl palaces in Paradise whose soil is musk.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي لله عنهما : له في الجنة ألف قصر من لؤلؤ أبيض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r5.claim: The lām before sawfa is an emphatic lām of initial assertion, requiring an implicit subject; it is not an oath lām, which requires nūn emphasis with a present verb.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r5.anchor: هي لام الابتداء المؤكدة لمضمون الجملة ، والمبتدأ محذوف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r6.claim: Combining emphatic lām with the future particle promises certain giving despite delay, because delay has wisdom.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r6.anchor: معناه أن العطاء كائن لا محالة وإن تأخر ، لما في التأخير من المصلحة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r4.claim: God may give the Prophet victory in this world and make the religion manifest, satisfying him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r4.anchor: يعطيك من النصر في الدنيا , وما يرضيك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r5.claim: Alternatively, God may give him a station and honor in the afterlife that satisfies him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r5.anchor: يعطيك المنزلة في الآخرة , وما يرضيك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#2/r1.claim: God will give the Prophet reward and intercessory standing in the hereafter; when the verse descended, he said he would not be satisfied while even one member of his community remained in the Fire.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#2/r1.anchor: ولما نزلت قال صلى الله عليه وسلم اذا لا أرضى قط وواحد من أمتى فى النار

NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#2/r2.claim: The lām before sawfa is an emphatic lām of initiation, with an implied subject and predicate; it cannot be a lām of oath because that requires an emphatic nūn before a present verb.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#2/r2.anchor: واللام الداخلة على سوف لام الابتداء المؤكدة لمضمون الجملة والمبتدأ محذوف تقديره ولانت سوف يعطيك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#2/r3.claim: The two emphatic particles combined with delayed fulfillment promise certain giving; earlier blessings are recounted to strengthen hope and patience for still greater good.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#2/r3.anchor: وذكر أن الجمع بين حرفى التأكيد والتأخير يؤذن بأن العطاء كائن لا محالة وان تأخر

QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet saw future conquests of his community and rejoiced, so Gabriel brought the promise of the afterlife and God’s gift.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أري النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما يفتح الله على أمته بعده فسر بذلك فنزل جبريل بقوله

QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r4.claim: One interpretation of God’s gift is the Pool and intercession.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r5.speaker: الأوزاعي، ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r5.claim: Al-Awzai raises from Ibn Abbas a report of a thousand white-pearl palaces with musk soil, each containing suitable spouses and servants.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: ألف قصر من لؤلؤ أبيض ترابه المسك. رفعه الأوزاعي

QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muhammad’s satisfaction is that none of his family enter Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r6.anchor: وعنه قال: رضي محمد ألا يدخل أحد من أهل بيته النار

QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r7.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r7.claim: Al-Suddi says the promised satisfaction is intercession for all believers.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r7.anchor: وقال السدي. وقيل: هي الشفاعة في جميع المؤمنين

QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r8.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r8.claim: Ali transmits the Prophet’s promise that God will allow his intercession for his community until He asks whether Muhammad is satisfied, and he says yes.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r8.anchor:
وعن علي رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" يشفعني الله في أمتي حتى يقول الله سبحانه لي

QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r9.claim: In Muslim, the Prophet prayed for his community and wept after reciting Abraham and Jesus’ prayers; God promised not to distress him concerning them.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r9.anchor:
وفي صحيح مسلم عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص:
" أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تلا قول الله تعالى في إبراهيم:

QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r10.claim: God promises to satisfy the Prophet concerning his community and not grieve him.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r10.anchor: إنا سنرضيك في أمتك ولا نسوءك

QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5#2/r1.speaker: أهل البيت
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5#2/r1.claim: The Prophet’s family say 93:5 is the most hopeful verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5#2/r1.anchor: قال: ولكنا أهل البيت نقول: إن أرجى آية في كتاب الله قوله تعالى: { ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى }

QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5#2/r2.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5#2/r2.claim: The Prophet reportedly said on revelation that he would not be satisfied while even one member of his community remained in the Fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5#2/r2.anchor:
وفي الحديث: لما نزلت هذه الآية قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" إذا والله لا أرضى وواحد من أمتي في النار

QUTB-ZILAL:93:5/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:5/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:5/r1.claim: God reserves what will satisfy the Prophet: success in his mission, removal of obstacles, victory of his way, and the emergence of truth—his concerns amid opposition, denial, harm, plotting, and mockery.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:5/r1.anchor: من التوفيق في دعوتك ، وإزاحة العقبات من طريقك ، وغلبة منهجك ، وظهور حقك

RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r1.claim: The promise is singular because the Prophet is its central recipient and believers follow him; honoring his companions honors him because he rejoices more in their reward than his own.

RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r2.claim: Other prophets say 'myself' to receive their reward before their nations, while Muhammad says 'my nation' because he longs to see them rewarded.
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r2.anchor: ومن ذلك حيث تقول الأنبياء : نفسي نفسي

RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r3.claim: When struck by opponents, the Prophet prayed for their guidance, but when the trench kept him from prayer he prayed against them; he accepted bodily injury, not injury to religion, so God exalted him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r3.anchor: حين شجوا وجهك ، قلت : ( اللهم اهد قومي فإنهم لا يعلمون )

RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r4.claim: Razi says God does not declare someone an unbeliever merely for years of missed prayer or preventing another's prayer, but does for harming even a hair or part of the Prophet's sandal.
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r4.anchor: فقلت من ترك الصلاة سنين ، أو حبس غيره عن الصلاة سنين لا أكفره

RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r5.claim: Using 'soon' means the Prophet's death is not near and he will live longer.
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r5.anchor: أنه يدل على أنه ما قرب أجله

RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r6.claim: The future promise answers the polytheists' claim that Muhammad would soon die, echoing God's earlier denial that He had abandoned or hated him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r6.anchor: ثم قال المشركون : سوف يموت محمد

RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r7.claim: Razi says Gabriel speaks the whole sura to the Prophet because he longed intensely for him and his speech, and God wanted Gabriel to give the good news.
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r7.anchor: هذه السورة من أولها إلى آخرها كلام جبريل عليه السلام معه

RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r8.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r8.claim: Al-Kashshaf calls the lām before sawfa emphatic lām of initiation; it cannot be an oath-lām without emphatic nūn, so an omitted subject is understood: 'You will surely be given.'
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r8.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : هي لام الابتداء المؤكدة

RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r9.claim: The paired emphasis and delay mean the gift is certain even if it comes later for a wise reason.
RAZI-FULL:v31p193/r9.anchor: معناه : أن العطاء كائن لا محالة ، وإن تأخر

RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r1.claim: The next verse specifies the extent of the afterlife's superiority: God's gift reaches the limit of what the Messenger desires and approves.
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r1.anchor: فبين بهذه الآية مقدار ذلك التفاوت

RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the afterlife is better because God grants everything the Prophet wants, beyond what worldly life can contain.
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r2.anchor: لأنه يعطيه كل ما يريده وذلك مما لا تتسع الدنيا له

RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the gift includes a thousand palaces of white pearl in Paradise, with musk for soil.
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r3.anchor: فقال ابن عباس : ألف قصر في الجنة من لؤلؤ أبيض

RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r4.claim: A report from Ali and Ibn Abbas identifies the gift as intercession for the community; the Prophet said he would not be satisfied while any follower remained in the Fire.
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r4.anchor: فالمروى عن علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام وابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r5.claim: Razi says intercession is the necessary reading: God commanded the Prophet to seek forgiveness for believers, and promising what pleases him entails granting that request for sinners.
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r5.anchor: واعلم أن الحمل على الشفاعة متعين

RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r6.claim: The preceding assurance fits intercession: God will not abandon or hate the Prophet, and will spare his companions, followers, and devotees from anger to please him and soothe his heart.
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r6.anchor: كأنه تعالى يقول لا أودعك ولا أبغضك

RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r7.claim: Numerous intercession reports show the Prophet is pleased when sinners are forgiven; combined with the promise to fulfill his pleasure, they establish intercession.
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r7.anchor: الأحاديث الكثيرة الواردة في الشفاعة دالة على أن رضا الرسول

RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r8.speaker: جعفر الصادق
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r8.claim: Jaʿfar al-Sadiq says his grandfather's satisfaction is that no monotheist enters the Fire.
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r8.anchor: وعن جعفر الصادق عليه السلام أنه قال : رضاء جدي

RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r9.speaker: الباقر
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r9.claim: Al-Baqir says the People of the House call this the most hopeful verse: it is intercession for monotheists until the Prophet says he is satisfied; others cite 39:53.
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r9.anchor: وعن الباقر ، أهل القرآن يقولون : أرجى آية

RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r10.claim: A worldly reading includes victories at Badr and Mecca, mass conversions, victory and expulsion of Jewish tribes, campaigns across Arabia, the caliphs' conquests, fallen empires, captured treasuries, and Islam's spread.
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r10.anchor: فهو إشارة إلى ما أعطاه الله تعالى من الظفر بأعدائه يوم بدر

RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r11.claim: Razi prefers to include blessings of both this world and the next.
RAZI-FULL:v31p192#2/r11.anchor: واعلم أن الأولى حمل الآية على خيرات الدنيا والآخرة

STUDYQURAN:93:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r1.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās relates that the Prophet asked for a favor, then God recalled blessings including shelter as an orphan, guidance, enrichment, an expanded breast, and a lifted burden.
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r1.anchor: Ibn ʿAbbās reported that the Prophet said, “I have asked my Lord for something I wish I had not asked for.

TAB-FULL:v24p488/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p488/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p488/r1.claim: God will grant Muḥammad abundant favors in the afterlife until he is satisfied.
TAB-FULL:v24p488/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} [الضحى: 5] : وذلك يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v24p488/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p488/r2.speaker: علي بن عبد الله بن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p488/r2.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās reports that the promise followed the conquests opened to the community and describes one thousand palaces in Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v24p488/r2.anchor: عن علي بن عبد الله بن عباس، عن أبيه، قال: عرض على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما هو مفتوح على أمته

TAB-FULL:v24p488/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p488/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p488/r3.claim: Qatāda says the giving occurs on the Day of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v24p488/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} [الضحى: 5] : وذلك يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v24p488/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p488/r4.speaker: السدي عن ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p488/r4.claim: A report attributed through al-Suddī to Ibn ʿAbbās says Muḥammad's satisfaction includes no member of his family entering Hell.
TAB-FULL:v24p488/r4.anchor: عن السدي، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} [الضحى: 5] قال: من رضا محمد

TABRISI:93:5/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:5/r13.claim: The oath response has no emphatic nūn because lām before sawfa already signals an oath, while the initial lām cannot precede a future particle.
TABRISI:93:5/r13.anchor: ولم يقل ويعطينك وإن كان جواب القسم لأن النون إنما تدخل

TABRISI:93:5/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:93:5/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says revelation ceased for fifteen days, prompting pagans to claim the Lord had abandoned and hated Muḥammad.
TABRISI:93:5/r16.anchor: وقيل: إنما احتبس الوحي اثني عشر يوما عن ابن جريج

TABRISI:93:5#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:5#2/r8.claim: God will give the Prophet intercession, the Pool, and other honors for him and his community until he is satisfied.
TABRISI:93:5#2/r8.anchor: معناه وسيعطيك ربك في الآخرة من الشفاعة والحوض وسائر أنواع الكرامة

TABRISI:93:5#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5#2/r9.speaker: محمد بن علي ابن الحنفية عن الحارث بن شريح
TABRISI:93:5#2/r9.claim: Al-Ḥārith transmits Muḥammad b. ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥanafiyya asking Iraqis about their claim to the most hopeful verse.
TABRISI:93:5#2/r9.anchor: وروى حرث بن شريح عن محمد بن علي ابن الحنفية أنه قال يا أهل العراق تزعمون

TABRISI:93:5#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5#2/r10.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:93:5#2/r10.claim: Muqātil gives forty days as the length of the revelation pause.

TABRISI:93:5#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:5#2/r11.claim: Another report says Muslims asked why revelation was not coming; the Prophet blamed their untrimmed nails and unclean knuckles, then told Gabriel he had missed him.
TABRISI:93:5#2/r11.anchor: وقيل: إن المسلمين قالوا ما ينزل عليك الوحي يا رسول الله

TABRISI:93:5#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5#2/r12.speaker: جبريل
TABRISI:93:5#2/r12.claim: Gabriel replies that he too longed for the Prophet but is a commanded servant who descends only when God orders.
TABRISI:93:5#2/r12.anchor: فقال جبرائيل ع: وأنا كنت أشد إليك شوقا ولكني عبد مأمور

TABRISI:93:5#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:5#2/r13.claim: A report says Jews asked about Dhū al-Qarnayn, the Cave Companions, and the Spirit; the Prophet promised to answer the next day without saying God willing, so the delay grieved him.
TABRISI:93:5#2/r13.anchor: وقيل: سألت اليهود رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ذي القرنين وأصحاب الكهف وعن الروح

TABRISI:93:5#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5#2/r14.speaker: أم جميل بنت حرب
TABRISI:93:5#2/r14.claim: Another story says a stone injured the Prophet's finger and revelation stopped for two or three nights; Umm Jamīl taunted him that his devil had left.
TABRISI:93:5#2/r14.anchor: فمكث ليلتين أو ثلاثا لا يوحى إليه فقالت له أم جميل بنت حرب امرأة أبي لهب

TABRISI:93:5-7/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5-7/r1.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:93:5-7/r1.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says the Prophet visited Fāṭima while she wore a coarse camel-hair cloak, ground grain, and nursed her child; he comforted her with the promised afterlife reward.
TABRISI:93:5-7/r1.anchor: وعليها كساء من ثلة الإبل وهي تطحن بيدها وترضع ولدها

TABRISI:93:5-7/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5-7/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي
TABRISI:93:5-7/r2.claim: Zayd b. ʿAlī says the Prophet's satisfaction includes admitting his family to Paradise.
TABRISI:93:5-7/r2.anchor: إن من رضا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يدخل أهل بيته الجنة

TABRISI:93:5-7/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5-7/r9.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:93:5-7/r9.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says the Prophet's satisfaction means no monotheist remains in the Fire.
TABRISI:93:5-7/r9.anchor: وقال الصادق ع: رضا جدي أن لا يبقى في النار موحد

TABRISI:93:5-7/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5-7/r10.speaker: أهل البيت
TABRISI:93:5-7/r10.claim: The Household identifies this as the most hopeful verse: the Prophet receives intercession for monotheists until he says he is satisfied.
TABRISI:93:5-7/r10.anchor: وإنا أهل البيت ع نقول أرجى آية في كتاب الله ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى وهي والله الشفاعة

THALABI:v10p222#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p222#3/r1.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v10p222#3/r1.claim: They report that Jews asked about Dhū al-Qarnayn, the Cave Companions, and the Spirit; the Prophet promised an answer the next day without saying “if God wills,” and revelation paused.
THALABI:v10p222#3/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: سألت اليهود رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ذي القرنين وأصحاب الكهف وعن الروح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p107/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p107/r1.speaker: unidentified report
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p107/r1.claim: An unassigned report describes a thousand white-pearl palaces whose soil is musk and that contain suitable furnishings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p107/r1.anchor: قال (¬1): ألف قصر من لؤلؤ أبيض، ترابه المسك، وفيهن ما يصلح لهن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p107/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p107/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p107/r2.claim: God will give the Prophet good things in the Hereafter, and he will be satisfied with what he receives.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p107/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعطيك ربك في الآخرة من الخير، فترضى بما يعطى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p107/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p107/r3.speaker: علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p107/r3.claim: Others interpret the promise as referring to intercession; ʿAlī is named as holding this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p107/r3.anchor: وذكر آخرون أن هذا في الشفاعة. وهو قول علي رضي الله عنه (¬4)

WAHIDI-QT:93:5/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:93:5/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:93:5/r1.claim: God will give Muhammad Hereafter reward and the station of intercession.
WAHIDI-QT:93:5/r1.anchor: { ولسوف يعطيك ربك } في الاخرة من الثواب وفي مقام الشفاعة

WAHIDI-QT:93:5/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:93:5/r2.speaker: عليه السلام
WAHIDI-QT:93:5/r2.claim: A report says Muhammad declared that he would not be satisfied while one member of his community remained in the Fire; no grading is stated.
WAHIDI-QT:93:5/r2.anchor: يروى أنه قال عليه السلام لما نزلت هذه الاية إذن لا أرضى وواحد من أمتي في النار

ELMALILI:93:5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5/r1.claim: The opening lām may be an emphatic introductory particle with an implied pronoun, or both lām and sawfa may be understood under an oath; both intensify the promise.
ELMALILI:93:5/r1.anchor: Bu lâm, وَلَلْءَاخِرَةُ gibi lâm-ı ibtidâ olarak وَلاََنْتَ سَوْفَ يـُعْطِيكَ رَبُّك takdîrinde olması da

ELMALILI:93:5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5/r2.claim: He says oath-based emphasis is stronger than the introductory lām alone.

ELMALILI:93:5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5/r3.claim: Sawfa marks a future event whose realization is certain.
ELMALILI:93:5/r3.anchor: “Sevfe” istikbalde tahakkuk[^1] ifade eden harf-i tenfistir

ELMALILI:93:5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5/r4.claim: Naming Rabb explicitly where a pronoun could stand renews the address and conveys successive tenderness through acts of lordly care.
ELMALILI:93:5/r4.anchor: رَبُّكَ isminin zamir yerinde izhârıyla hitâbın iadesi rubûbiyet tecelliyâtının tevâlîsiyle taltif üzerine taltiftir

ELMALILI:93:5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5/r5.claim: God will give so abundantly that the Prophet reaches complete contentment, with no grief, distress, or waiting left in the enduring afterlife.
ELMALILI:93:5/r5.anchor: tamamen râzı olacak, rızâya ereceksin bütün dileklerin husûle gelecek

ELMALILI:93:5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5/r6.claim: This contentment is higher than the station of being content and approved: in divine beauty, all the soul's inclinations unfold toward fulfillment.
ELMALILI:93:5/r6.anchor: Bu atânın istikbal sîgasıyla ifade edilmesine nazaran kemâl-i uhrevî bir va‘d-i kerîm olduğunda şüphe yoksa da

ELMALILI:93:5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5/r7.claim: The promise also includes worldly gifts: spiritual openings, knowledge, success in proclaiming truth, the Hijra, the conquest of Mecca, and Islam's spread.
ELMALILI:93:5/r7.anchor: dünyadaki füyûzât-ı nefsiye, ulûm-i evvelîn ve âhirîne vukuf

ELMALILI:93:5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5/r8.claim: Its greatest importance is the afterlife, where true contentment belongs and recompense is fully given.
ELMALILI:93:5/r8.anchor: uhreviyede olacağından va‘d u atânın asıl ehemmiyeti de ondadır

ELMALILI:93:5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r9.speaker: حسن
ELMALILI:93:5/r9.claim: Hasan interprets the promised gift as intercession.
ELMALILI:93:5/r9.anchor: İbn Ebî Hâtim’in Hasan’dan tahrîcinde هِيَ الشَّفَاعَة demiştir

ELMALILI:93:5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r10.speaker: علي
ELMALILI:93:5/r10.claim: Ali transmits that the Prophet will intercede for his community until God asks whether he is satisfied; the Ahl al-Bayt identify this verse as intercession.
ELMALILI:93:5/r10.anchor: Muhammed b. Hanefiyye, Ali keremallahu veche’den bana tahdis eyledi ki

ELMALILI:93:5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ELMALILI:93:5/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says one form of the Prophet's satisfaction is that no member of his household enter the Fire.
ELMALILI:93:5/r11.anchor: İbn Cerîr’in İbn Abbas’tan tahrîcinde; bu âyette demiştir ki

ELMALILI:93:5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ELMALILI:93:5/r12.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas defines the Prophet's satisfaction as his entire community entering Paradise.
ELMALILI:93:5/r12.anchor: ondan diğer vechile rivayetinde ise onun rızâsı ümmetinin hepsinin cennete girmesidir

ELMALILI:93:5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5/r13.claim: The Prophet's deep compassion for his community supports these readings of his satisfaction.
ELMALILI:93:5/r13.anchor: Aleyhissalatü vesselâm’ın ümmetine karşı büyük şefkatinin muktezâsı da budur

ELMALILI:93:5/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r14.speaker: محمد
ELMALILI:93:5/r14.claim: A report says the Prophet recited Abraham's prayer for followers and Jesus' appeal concerning his people, raised his hands weeping, and prayed for his community; God promised to please him.
ELMALILI:93:5/r14.anchor: İki elini kaldırdı da اَللّٰهُمَّ أُمَّتِي أُمَّتِي dedi ve ağladı

ELMALILI:93:5/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5/r15.claim: The Prophet can only be pleased with what pleases God; intercession requires divine permission, and God is not pleased with disbelief.
ELMALILI:93:5/r15.anchor: Peygamber’in rızâsı Allah’ın rızâsındadır. Allah’ın rızâsı olmayan bir hususa Peygamber’in râzı olması

ELMALILI:93:5/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5/r16.claim: The intercession report for major sinners encourages no sin; the word 'my community' establishes the value of faith and following, and excludes disbelief.
ELMALILI:93:5/r16.anchor: de kebâire teşvik için değil, “ümmetî” izâfetiyle iman ve ittibâ‘nisbetinin kıymetini

ELMALILI:93:5/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5/r17.claim: Even unbelievers may benefit from Muhammad's gifts in this world, but without faith that benefit ends here and the afterlife brings loss and severe punishment.
ELMALILI:93:5/r17.anchor: bu istifade imana iktiran etmedikçe dünyada kalır. Âhiret için hüsran ve azâb-ı azîm olur

ELMALILI:93:5#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r1.claim: The promise does not mean the Prophet should seek indiscriminate forgiveness or demand that Hell be closed; that would promote disbelief and injustice and misuse compassion.
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r1.anchor: herkes hakkında bir afv-ı umûmî ilânını istemeli ve cehennemi bütün bütün kapattırmadan râzı olmamalıydı

ELMALILI:93:5#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r2.claim: No one may speak before the Merciful without permission and speaking rightly; the cited verse limits intercession accordingly.
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r2.anchor: hak ve savab söylemeyenlerin huzûr-ı Rahmân’da tekellüme hakk u salâhiyetleri yoktur

ELMALILI:93:5#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r3.claim: The universal forgiveness in 39:53 includes disbelief and association, but its following command summons people to repent, submit, and believe; Islam erases past sins.
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r3.anchor: bu afv-ı umûmî âyeti, arkasındaki وَأَنِيبُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ وَأَسْلِمُوا۟ hitâbıyla

ELMALILI:93:5#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r4.claim: The forgiveness promise is not an invitation to sin; stubborn unbelievers who never repent have no share in it, and neither God nor the Prophet would seek to quench their earned punishment.
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r4.anchor: Yoksa zünûb ve me‘âsîye teşvik için değildir. Allah ve Peygamber tanımayan

ELMALILI:93:5#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r5.claim: The previous surah warns that those who deny the good and turn away are eased toward hardship and blazing Fire; this surah's exclusive good for the Prophet warns against them.
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r5.anchor: evvelki sûrede وَأَمَّا مَنۢ بَخِلَ وَٱسْتَغْنَىٰ وَكَذَّبَ بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ

ELMALILI:93:5#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r6.claim: Those who follow the Prophet belong to him, as Abraham's statement about his followers illustrates.

ELMALILI:93:5#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r7.claim: Intercession is a central part of Muhammad's gift, and each community member's share is proportionate to following him.
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r7.anchor: bu atâ-i Muhammedîde ümmete şefaat kaziyyesi pek mühim bir asıldır

ELMALILI:93:5#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r8.speaker: أبو حيان
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r8.claim: The gift should be read broadly to include worldly favors and the many kinds of afterlife gifts, with the latter far greater.
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r8.anchor: demişlerdir ki evlâ olan dünyevî atıyyelere de, türlü envâ‘ıyla uhrevî atıyyelere de umûmudur

ELMALILI:93:5#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r9.claim: The Prophet can trust that each later stage will be better than the last; the blessings described next demonstrate this pattern.
ELMALILI:93:5#2/r9.anchor: olduğu kaziyyesine itmi‘nânı takrir için daha evvelinden meşhud olan ni‘am-i celîle

CORPUSCORANICUM:93:5:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:93:5:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:93:5:anmerkung/r1.claim: The root r-ḍ-y has eschatological connotations, while the verse also resembles Psalm 20:5’s non-eschatological wish that God grant one’s desire and fulfill one’s plans.
CORPUSCORANICUM:93:5:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zum gesamten Vers vgl. die allerdings nicht eschatologisch zu deutende Verheißung in Psalm 20:5

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r3.claim: The author prefers the first reading: against claims that revelation had stopped and Muhammad's cause would fail, God promises his future prophetic work will be spiritually and practically more fruitful.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r3.anchor: bundan sonraki hayatının, peygamberlik faaliyetlerinin ruhanî tekâmülünün öncekinden daha verimli, daha başarılı olacağını müjdelemiştir

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p231/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p231/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p231/r2.claim: The Prophet was shown the conquests opening for his community village by village and rejoiced; then the promise of God's giving until he is satisfied was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p231/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال عرض على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما هو مفتوح على أمته كفرا كفرا أي قرية قرية فسر به

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p458/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p458/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p458/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet rejoiced when shown his community's future conquests, so these verses were revealed; he was promised a thousand pearl palaces in Paradise, each with its provisions of spouses and servants.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p458/r1.anchor: علي بن عبد الله بن عباس، عن أبيه قال: رأى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ما يفتح على أمته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p412/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p412/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p412/r4.claim: Sawfa marks the future, like the preceding promise, and the lām in wa-lasawfa repeats its emphasis.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p412/r4.anchor: وجاء أيضاً باللام في (ولسوف) وأكده بنفس التوكيد باللام

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p413/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p413/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p413/r1.claim: God leaves both gift and contentment unrestricted, names Himself as the Lord, and addresses the Prophet personally; each choice magnifies the honor and scope of the gift.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p413/r1.anchor: أطلق سبحانه العطاء ولم يحدده إنما شمل هذا العطاء كل شيء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p413/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p413/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p413/r2.claim: Contentment is among life’s greatest blessings: it brings peace and stability, while lack of it makes wealth, comfort, or ease feel like hardship and deprivation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p413/r2.anchor: الرضى هو من أجل النعم على الإنسان وهو أساس الاستقرار والطمأنينة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r4.claim: The majority place the promised gift in the Hereafter; Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet is satisfied when none of his household enter Hell, and elsewhere describes a thousand palaces with their provisions and servants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r4.anchor: ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى، قال الجمهور: ذلك في الآخرة. وقال ابن عباس: رضاه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r5.claim: A view placing the gift in this world, such as the conquest of Mecca, can be included; the promise best encompasses both worldly victories and stored reward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r5.anchor: وقيل: في الدنيا بفتح مكة وغيره، والأولى أن هذا موعد شامل لما أعطاه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p159/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159/r1.claim: The emphatic laam in ولسوف يعطيك has been explained by positing a deleted subject ('you will surely receive'); critics object that emphasis conflicts with deleting its subject, but Alusi replies that deleting a subject is common and may be grammatical rather than semantic.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159/r1.anchor: وقالوا فائدتها تأكيد مضمون لجملة وبعدها مبتدأ محذوف أي ولأنت سوف يعطيك الخ وأورد عليه أن التأكيد يقتضي الأعتناء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p159/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159/r2.speaker: ابن الحاجب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159/r2.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib argues that an emphasized subject should not be deleted, comparing the laam with qad before verbs and inna before nouns; Alusi says this does not settle the issue against al-Fārisī and others.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159/r2.anchor: ولذا قال ابن الحاجب أن المبتدأ المؤكد باللام لا يحذف وأن اللام مع المبتدأ كقد مع الفعل وأن مع الاسم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p159/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159/r3.claim: A second grammatical possibility treats the laam as emphasizing the whole assertion; it need not necessarily convert the following imperfect to present time, and if it does, سوف can signal a certain gift delayed for wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159/r3.anchor: واللام المؤكدة لا نسلم أنها لتخليص المضارع للحال أيضا بل هي لمطلق التأكيد فقط

ALUSI-FULL:v30p159/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159/r4.claim: Some grammarians take both laams as oath particles and the conjunction as joining two promises to the oath; Alusi finds this attractive, and the objection that an oath requires nūn is answered by accepted exceptions after a future marker and in coordinated clauses.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159/r4.anchor: وذهب بعضهم بأن اللام الأولى للقسم وكذا هذه اللام وبقسميتها جزم غير واحد فالواو عليه للعطف فكلا الوعدين داخل في المقسم عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r1.claim: Although some grammarians require an emphatic nūn after an oath laam, others exempt verbs accompanied by سوف, intervening complements, or present-tense verbs; nūn may also be omitted in a coordinated clause. Alusi says this makes the oath reading less problematic.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r1.anchor: وكذا مع فصل معمول بين اللام والفعل نحو ولئن متم أو قتلتم لإلى الله تحشرون

ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r2.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r2.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn takes the preceding denial as circumstantial: the Hereafter is better for the Prophet, so his Lord would not abandon him; the promise then means He will give him the Hereafter. Alusi objects that the paired laams and oath make this reading unlikely and its paraphrase is strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r2.anchor: الأظهر أن جملة ما ودعك حالية أي ما ودعك ربك وما قلاك والحال أن الآخرة خير لك من الأولى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r3.claim: One view makes the promise encompass both worldly gifts—perfection, knowledge, victories and spreading Islam—and afterlife honors; another limits it to the Hereafter, while also recognizing Meccan conquest among worldly gifts.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r3.anchor: واختلف في قوله تعالى ولسوف الخ فقيل هو عدة كريمة شاملة لما أعطاه الله عز وجل في الدنيا من كمال النفس وعلوم الأولين والآخرين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r4.claim: The majority take the promise as referring to the Hereafter.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r4.anchor: والجمهور على أنه عدة أخروية فأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الحسن أنه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r1.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the promised gift is intercession.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r1.anchor: قال هي الشفاعة وروي نحوه عن بعض أهل البيت رضي الله تعالى عنهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r2.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r2.claim: A report from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya, via ʿAlī, says the Prophet will intercede until God asks whether he is pleased; the Prophet answers yes. The report calls intercession the most hopeful verse for the Prophet's family.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r2.anchor: من طريق حرب بن شريح قال قلت لأبي جعفر محمد بن علي بن الحسين على جدهم وعليهم الصلاة والسلام أرأيت

ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r3.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r3.claim: Jābir reports that the Prophet saw Fāṭima grinding grain in a camel-hide cloak and urged her to endure worldly hardship for tomorrow's reward; this supports a broader reading of the promised gifts.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r3.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال دخل رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم على فاطمة وهي تطحن بالرحا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers a general promise encompassing all kinds of reward in this life and the next; the afterlife gifts remain much greater.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r4.anchor: وقال أبو حيان الولى العموم لما في الدنيا والآخرة على اختلاف أنواعه والخبر المذكور لو سلم صحته لا يأبى ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r5.claim: One report says God grants him a thousand pearl palaces in Paradise, each with suitable spouses and servants.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r5.anchor: فقد روي الحاكم وصححه وجماعة عن ابن عباس أنه قال أعطاه الله تعالى في الجنة ألف قصر من لؤلؤ

ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet's satisfaction includes no member of his family entering Hell; another report says his pleasure is to bring his whole community into Paradise.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عنه أنه قال في الآية من رضا محمد صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أن لا يدخل أحد من أهل بيته النار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r7.claim: A further report from Ibn ʿAbbās says Muhammad and no one of his community will be left in the Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r7.anchor: وفي رواية الخطيب في تلخيص المتشابه من وجه آخر عنه لا يرضى محمد صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وأحد من أمته في النار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r8.claim: Muslim reports that the Prophet recited Abraham's and Jesus's prayers for their followers, raised his hands for his community and wept; God sent Gabriel to promise that He would please him concerning them and not grieve him.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r8.anchor: وقد أخرج مسلم كما في الدر المنثور عن ابن عمر أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم تلا قول الله تعالى في إبراهيم عليه السلام فمن تبعني فإنه مني

ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r9.claim: Repeating 'your Lord' with the possessive pronoun adds a clear tenderness to the promise.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p160/r9.anchor: وفي إعادة اسم الرب مع إضافته إلى ضميره عليه الصلاة والسلام ما لا يخفى أيضا من اللطف به

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r1.claim: According to Ibn Abbas, with Ali and Hasan agreeing, the promised gift is intercession for the Prophet's community until he is satisfied.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r1.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: هو الشفاعة في أمته حتى يرضى، وهو قول علي والحسن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r2.claim: He reports that the Prophet wept, praying for his community, and God promised through Gabriel to satisfy him concerning them and not grieve him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "اللهم أمتي أمتي وبكى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r3.claim: Abu Jaafar contrasts Iraqis' choice of 39:53 as the most hopeful verse with the Prophet's family choosing this verse for its promised reward.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r3.anchor: وقال حرب بن شريح سمعت أبا جعفر محمد بن علي يقول: إنكم يا معشر أهل العراق تقولون: أرجى آية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes the gift to mean victory, empowerment, and a large number of believers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r4.anchor: وقيل: من النصر والتمكين وكثرة المؤمنين

BAYDAWI-FULL:93:4-5/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:4-5/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:4-5/r2.claim: After promising continuing revelation and honor in this life, God promises the Prophet an even greater afterlife gift, including perfection, triumph, and elevation of the religion.
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:4-5/r2.anchor: وعد له ما هو أعلى وأجل من ذلك في الآخرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:93:4-5/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:4-5/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:4-5/r3.claim: The promise embraces what God gave him and what was stored for him beyond comprehension; the lām is emphatic, not an oath, and its conjunction with سوف guarantees delayed fulfillment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:4-5/r3.anchor: وجمعها مع سوف للدلالة على أن الإعطاء كائن لا محالة وإن تأخر

BINTSHATI:v1p36/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r1.claim: The surah is among the earliest revelations and came in Mecca years before the Hijra.
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r1.anchor: وسورة الضحى من أوائل الوحي، نزلت بمكة قبل الهجرة بسنين

BINTSHATI:v1p36/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r2.claim: The apparent pause in revelation was natural, like night settling after the dawn's brightness.
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r2.anchor: أن فتور الوحي ظاهرة طبيعية، شأنها شأن سجو الليل بعد إشراق الضحى

BINTSHATI:v1p36/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r3.claim: The Quran gives neither a cause nor duration for the pause; proposed explanations and counts of twelve to forty days add nothing to its central meaning.
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r3.anchor: فلأن الذي يعنيه هو جوهر الموقف لا تفصيلاته الجزئية

BINTSHATI:v1p36/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r5.claim: The promised good confirms that God has not abandoned or hated the Prophet and comforts him after the pause.
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r5.anchor: وقد أكد الله بهذا الخير الموعود، نفى التوديع والقلى، ليذهب عن رسوله أثر فتور الوحي

BINTSHATI:v1p39/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r1.claim: A reported interpretation specifies a thousand pearl palaces whose earth is musk, with another report describing them as white pearls.
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r1.anchor: ألف قصر من لؤلؤ، ترابهن المسك، وفيهن ما يصلحهن. عن إبن عباس أيضاً

BINTSHATI:v1p39/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r2.claim: Fixing the gift at a thousand or a million palaces, of any jewel or soil, constrains the Quran's promise, whose wording extends until complete satisfaction.
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r2.anchor: وما أرى ألف قصر في الجنة، أو ألف ألف، من لؤلؤ أو غير لؤلؤ

BINTSHATI:v1p39/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r3.speaker: آخرون
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r3.claim: Others read the gift as victory over enemies, the conquest of Mecca, mass conversion, and major conquests by the caliphs.
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r3.anchor: ذهبوا في تفسير العطاء إلى أنه إشارة إلى ما سوف يعطى الله رسوله من الظفر بأعدائه

BINTSHATI:v1p39/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r4.speaker: قيل
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r4.claim: Another view identifies the gift as intercession and forgiveness for the Prophet's followers, supported by reports about intercession and his satisfaction when their requests are answered.
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r4.anchor: لأن الله أمره بالاستغفار للمذنبين، ويرضيه - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أن يجاب طلبه.

BINTSHATI:v1p39/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r5.speaker: إبن القيم
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r5.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim rejects the claim that the Prophet cannot be satisfied while any follower remains in Hell: he accepts God's judgment and intercedes only with divine permission.
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r5.anchor: فإنه صلوات الله وسلامه عليه، يرضى بما يرضى به تبارك وتعالى

BINTSHATI:v1p39/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r6.speaker: إبن القيم
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r6.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim instead takes the gift broadly to include Quran, guidance, followers, renown, victory, and what Muhammad receives after death.
BINTSHATI:v1p39/r6.anchor: فهو يعم ما في الدنيا من القرآن والهدى والصر وكثرة الأتباع

BINTSHATI:v1p40/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p40/r1.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v1p40/r1.claim: Muhammad Abduh condemns importing discussions of intercession and the Prophet's family into this tafsir as alien to the Quran's religious spirit.
BINTSHATI:v1p40/r1.anchor: ما للمفسرين هنا من كلام في الشفاعة، وفي تكريم آل بيت النبوة، حشروه في التفسير حشراً

BINTSHATI:v1p40/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p40/r2.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v1p40/r2.claim: Abduh explains the gift as continuing revelation, guidance for Muhammad and his people, the spread of Islam, and their elevation in both worlds.
BINTSHATI:v1p40/r2.anchor: توارد الوحي عليك بما فيه إرشاد لك ولقومك، ومن ظهور دينك وعلو كلمنك

BINTSHATI:v1p40/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p40/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p40/r3.claim: Specifying the gift does the verse an injustice; the grandeur of the promise is best preserved by leaving satisfaction beyond every limit and description.
BINTSHATI:v1p40/r3.anchor: والأليق بجلال الموقف أن يكتفي فيه بالرضى على ما أراد البيان القرآني، فوق كل تحديد

BINTSHATI:v1p40/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p40/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p40/r4.claim: To solve the grammatical objection to the laam before sawfa, al-Zamakhshari posits an omitted subject: the original construction would say that you will be given.
BINTSHATI:v1p40/r4.anchor: من تقدير مبتدأ محذوف، وأن يكون أصل العبارة:

BINTSHATI:v1p40/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p40/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v1p40/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan likewise calls the laam an introductory emphatic particle and supplies an omitted subject, أنت.
BINTSHATI:v1p40/r5.anchor: إن اللام هنا لام إبتداء أكدت مضمون الجملة على إضمار مبتدأ أي:

BINTSHATI:v1p41/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p41/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p41/r1.claim: Grammatical rules should be tested against the Quranic expression as the primary witness, rather than forcing an imagined original wording onto it.
BINTSHATI:v1p41/r1.anchor: وكان يكفي أن يأتي التعبير في الكتاب العربي المبين، ليكون هو الشاهد والحجة

BINTSHATI:v1p41/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p41/r2.speaker: مفسرون
BINTSHATI:v1p41/r2.claim: Some commentators ask how emphatic laam can accompany the future-marking sawfa, then answer that the gift is certain even if delayed for a benefit.
BINTSHATI:v1p41/r2.anchor: كيف يجتمع التوكيد المستفاد من اللام، مع التسويف الصريح في {سَوْفَ} ؟

BINTSHATI:v1p41/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p41/r3.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v1p41/r3.claim: Abduh links sawfa to the fact that completion of the religion took twenty years, citing the verse announcing that Islam was completed.
BINTSHATI:v1p41/r3.anchor: إن إكمال الدين لم يتم إلا في عشرين سنة

BINTSHATI:v1p41/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p41/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p41/r4.claim: Emphasis on the future is ordinary Arabic; sawfa reassures Muhammad that God's care would continue through his past and future, his earlier and later life.
BINTSHATI:v1p41/r4.anchor: إيناساً للرسول المصطفى بأنه كان سوف يظل موضععناية ربه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r5.claim: The initial lām plus sawfa promises that the gift will certainly come despite a purposeful delay; this is not an oath construction.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r5.anchor: وضم هذه اللام إلى كلمة التنفيس للدلالة على أن العطاء وإن تأخر وقته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r6.claim: The promised gift includes knowledge, the triumph of religion, conquests, the fall of empires, lawful spoils, and the Prophet's generous giving.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r6.anchor: من كمال العلم وظهور الأمر وإعلاء الدين وفتح البلاد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r7.claim: It also includes the Hereafter's Praiseworthy Station, the Pool, and the great intercession.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r7.anchor: المقام المحمود والحوض المورود , والشفاعة العظمىة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r8.claim: The language allows four responses: receiving with satisfaction, being denied and dissatisfied, receiving without satisfaction, or being denied yet content.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r8.anchor: معطى راض , وممنوع غير راض , ومعطى غير راض , وممنوع راض

BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r9.speaker: علي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r9.claim: ʿAlī calls this the Qurʾān's most hope-giving verse because Muḥammad will not accept any member of his community remaining in Hell.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r9.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه أناه أرجى آية في القرآن

DURR-FULL:v8p542/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r1.claim: Through al-Suddi, Ibn Abbas says the Prophet will be satisfied when none of his household enters the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r1.anchor: من طريق السدي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} قال: من رضا محمد أن لا يدخل أحد من أهل بيته النار

DURR-FULL:v8p542/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r2.claim: Through Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Ibn Abbas says the Prophet's satisfaction is for his whole community to enter Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r2.anchor: من طريق سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} قال: رضاه أن تدخل أمته الجنة كلهم

DURR-FULL:v8p542/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r3.claim: Another report says Muhammad will not be content with even one member of his community remaining in the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} قال: لا يرضى محمد واحد من أمته في النار

DURR-FULL:v8p542/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r4.speaker: الله
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r4.claim: After the Prophet prayed and wept for his community, God told Gabriel He would satisfy Muhammad concerning them and not grieve him.
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r4.anchor: فقال الله: يا جبريل اذهب إلى محمد فقل له: إنا سنرضيك في أمتك ولا نسوءك

DURR-FULL:v8p542/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r5.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r5.claim: Ali's report says the Prophet will intercede until God asks whether he is satisfied and he answers yes.
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r5.anchor: عن علي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: أشفع لأمتي حتى يناديني ربي أرضيت يا محمد

DURR-FULL:v8p542/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r6.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the promised gift as intercession.
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r6.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه أنه سئل عن قوله: {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} قال: هي الشفاعة

DURR-FULL:v8p542/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r7.claim: Ibn Masud transmits the Prophet's words that God chose the Hereafter for his household over this world, followed by the verse.
DURR-FULL:v8p542/r7.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إنا أهل بيت اختار الله لنا الآخرة على الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v8p543/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r1.claim: When he saw Fatima grinding grain in a coarse camel-hair cloak, the Prophet urged her to endure worldly hardship for the Hereafter's bliss; the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: دخل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على فاطمة وهي تطحن بالرحى

DURR-FULL:v8p543/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r2.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r2.claim: After ‘the Hereafter is better,’ al-Abbas says God would leave His Prophet among the people only briefly because what follows is better for him.
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه قال: لما نزلت {وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى} قال العباس بن عبد المطلب

DURR-FULL:v8p543/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r3.claim: He says the gift that brings the Prophet's satisfaction is Paradise on the Day of Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} قال: ذلك يوم القيامة هي الجنة

DURR-FULL:v8p544/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p544/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p544/r2.claim: After the Sura al-Duha was revealed, the Prophet said that his Lord favors him and is worthy to favor him.
DURR-FULL:v8p544/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: لما نزلت {والضحى} على رسو ل الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#3/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#3/r1.speaker: author
